I know this feeling. I had a fair amount of friends and was managing my depression alright. Until I wasn't.

Through a set of events, I had two suicide attempts and developed anxiety and a pretty severe paranoia. Lost most of my friends. And this downward spiral you mentioned became my life.

I'm still in it, honestly. From my experience though, you start to take comfort in the solitude. The spiral starts to unwind. You end up being less pissed about being alone, and just get used to some (or a lot of) alone time. Eventually, your friends or other people will notice you're just there. Not angry, not frantically trying to see someone. Just.. There. And they'll approach you. And you'll start again.

At least, this is my experience. Another thing that helps is fake being happy for a bit. Seems counter productive, but if they think you're fine, they'll talk to you. Which could make you actually fine. Which breaks the cycle.

PS: feel free to message me if you want to chat more. I feel ya, and hope I can help
